rows.why: Item 2 asks how much case and whitespace cleaning is done before matching. The pick trims and lowercases, and readStatus("  PUBLISHED  ") returned 'published'. So "Draft", " PUBLISHED ", "Merged" and "claimed" all read as their canonical status, as S1 expects.

Item 4 asks which old spellings count as known legacy values. The pick maps only "in review" to review, and the run shows "done" reading as null. So "under_review" and "LIVE" would read as null, but S2 expects "review" and "published" and lists many more legacy spellings.

Item 1 asks what an unmatched stored value returns. The pick returns null and never guesses the nearest status (readStatus("archived") → null). Item 10 shows empty and whitespace-only values also read as null. This matches S3's 'no status, never the nearest one'.
No item asks whether an exact canonical value is stored unchanged on write. Item 5 is only about non-canonical values, so answering it would not settle what S4 expects.

Item 5 asks whether writing accepts non-canonical but readable values, including old spellings. The pick accepts only exact enum strings, and "Draft", "in-review", " draft" and "in review" all threw. Item 6 confirms the error message quotes the value as given ("\" Draft \" is not a sandbox status"), which covers the rest of S5.

Item 8 asks how the batch read reports unreadable values. The pick returns a list of distinct raw values, exactly as stored and sorted, and the run returned [ 'Alpha', 'Bogus', 'alpha', 'zeta ' ]. Item 7 confirms each unreadable row is kept with status null. Both match S6.
